# Generated default, review before merging. Every path below is published to a
# public site. Keep only what the site needs at run time; see the notes after this one.
#
# Publish list for GitHub Pages.
#
# This file decides what becomes public. The deploy workflow reads it,
# publishes ONLY the paths named here, and stops (leaving the previous live
# site up) if anything is wrong. It belongs to the project: the team template
# sync creates it when it is missing and never overwrites it.
#
# A change to this file changes what is public, so the security reviewer
# checks every pull request that touches it.
#
# One entry per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#
#   /index.html        Publishes one file. The leading slash is required; it
#                      anchors the path to the repository root.
#   /assets/           A trailing slash publishes that whole folder.
#   !/assets/old-*.js  Never publish matching paths, even inside a published
#                      folder. Wildcards are allowed only on ! lines.
#   require /VERSION   This file must exist, and not be empty, in the finished
#                      site and on the live site. It publishes nothing by
#                      itself: list the file or its folder as well.
#
# Not allowed, and the deploy fails with a message naming the line: a path
# without a leading slash, "..", spaces, wildcards on an include line, and
# /tests/ as includes. Also not allowed on an include or require line: a name
# that starts with a dot (the upload step drops hidden files, so it would
# never publish), and a symbolic link.
#
# Test files (*.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/) and node_modules never publish,
# whatever is listed here. The deploy also fails if a tests folder, a key file
# (*.pem, *.key, *.p12, id_rsa*) or a symbolic link ends up in the site.
#
# The lines below are the canonical static front-end layout. Remove folders
# the project does not have; add a line for any other runtime path (for
# example /fonts/ or /VERSION), and a require line for runtime files that sit
# inside a whole-folder entry. The first line keeps the team shell scripts
# that the template sync puts in scripts/ out of the public site.
!/scripts/*.sh
/index.html
/scripts/
require /index.html
